text:
The Calgary Herald's Steinberg column says Craig Conroy's patience is paying off with Adam Klapka. The undrafted Czech winger had a goal and an assist in a 2-1 win in San Jose on Nov. 2, and KSAT's headline credited the fourth-line wingers for backing Dustin Wolf. He has 6 points in 17 games, a third of his total from all of last season.

He plays 11 minutes a night and throws 58 hits, which is the job. His finishing is a little ahead of schedule (3 goals on 2.12 expected), and his points rate of 1.85 per 60 is above the range we'd expect. The on-ice share is the weak spot: Calgary takes 45% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him at five on five.

His tools are better than his role suggests. His shot is in the 95th percentile for speed and his skating is quick (88th percentile top speed). He came up through the Calgary Wranglers after signing as a free agent and played for Czechia at the 2025 World Championship. We project about 13 goals. On a Flames team searching for scoring, a fourth-liner chipping in is a bonus they need.
headline: Klapka is thriving on the fourth line
